name: Fernbrook Outfitters
_note: Benchmark application 1. Excluded from nothing; the Deep fixture is the one excluded from transfer evaluation. Regions are named so assertions never contain a CSS selector, which lets the DOM be restructured without rewriting the fault library.

faults.description: The order confirmation reports the number of distinct basket lines as the quantity, rather than the quantity actually ordered. A single-line order of five units confirms as one unit.
faults.trigger_condition: Open a product, set a quantity of 2 or more, add it to the basket, continue to checkout, supply a valid email and postcode, and confirm the order.
faults.expected_behaviour: The confirmation echoes the quantity the user entered on the product page.
faults.observable_violation: The quantity cell on the confirmation shows a different number from the one entered. The page returns 200, logs nothing, and the basket one step earlier showed the correct number.

assertions.describes: the confirmation's quantity cell must echo the quantity entered on the product page

faults._horizon_note: The triggering action (setting the quantity) is three state transitions before the page where the violation becomes observable: product -> basket -> checkout -> confirmation. Documented because H >= 3 may be useful for a delayed-credit study later; that experiment is deferred and this fixture was not designed for it.

faults.description: The checkout declares that a delivery postcode is required, but the guard is not enforced, so an order can be placed with the postcode field left empty.
faults.trigger_condition: Reach the checkout with a non-empty basket, enter a valid email, leave the postcode empty, and confirm the order.
faults.expected_behaviour: Confirming with an empty postcode is refused and the validation warning is shown.
faults.observable_violation: The confirmation page is reached, and the delivery postcode it shows is empty.

assertions.describes: with an empty postcode the guard must refuse the order, so the run must still be on the checkout page when it ends
the confirmation displays a blank delivery postcode, because the order was committed without one

faults._assertion_note: Stated as expected behaviour, which is how this grammar works. Conjunct 1: the guard should keep the run on checkout.html, so the violation is the final step being elsewhere. Conjunct 2: the confirmation renders a blank delivery postcode, which is only possible if the order was committed without one. Scoped to confirmation.html, so a run that never got there is inconclusive rather than a false positive. Two earlier drafts were inverted -- url_matches and text_contains both mean 'must', so neither fires when the thing is present.

characterization.workflow_state_representation: sessionStorage, not the URL query string
characterization._contrast_with_deep_fixture: The deep-flow fixture carries flow state in the query string and gates each stage by revealing a hidden Continue link. This application keeps workflow state in sessionStorage so it is invisible in the URL, uses a table-driven catalogue rather than a linear wizard, and gates on form validation rather than on link reveal. Vocabulary, DOM idiom (semantic sectioning and class hooks rather than ids everywhere) and visual style are all different.
